Referral Note

39-year-old married accountant with worsening anxiety over the past year. Reports excessive worry nearly every day for approximately 10 months, spanning finances, work performance, his children's health, family safety, his parents' health, home maintenance, and future illness. He recognizes the worry as excessive but cannot stop anticipating worst-case outcomes. Associated sleep-onset insomnia, muscle tension, fatigue, irritability, impaired concentration, and restlessness. Spouse reports constant reassurance-seeking. Medical evaluation unrevealing apart from well-controlled hypertension. Referring for psychiatric evaluation and treatment planning.

Behavioral Observations (on arrival)

Appearance: Appropriately dressed and well groomed. Appears stated age.

Behavior: Cooperative and engaged. Appears mildly anxious; fidgets frequently throughout the interview. Asks more than once whether he is answering correctly.

Speech: Normal rate, rhythm, and volume.

Mood / Affect: Describes mood as “constantly worried”; affect anxious but appropriate and congruent.

Thought / Perception: Logical, linear, goal-directed. Content notable for excessive worry across multiple domains. No delusions, obsessions, or perceptual disturbances. Denies SI/HI.

Cognition / Insight: Alert, oriented ×4. Insight and judgment intact; he identifies the worry as excessive.
